category_title: Passive classroom bystanders who engage through personal narratives and experimental design
minimal_context: The student is participating in a freshman biology group investigation to test environmental impacts on plants.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's review your group's plan for testing environmental impacts on the plants.

STUDENT: I tried to give suggestions for a more authentic study design. In middle school science classes, we did real hands-on experiments, but here they just want to pour Windex on the plants.

TUTOR: What did your group members say when you shared your idea?

STUDENT: My suggestions were dismissed by my classmates.

TUTOR: Well, try to keep participating and working with your group.

STUDENT: (Becomes a silent bystander, limiting her interactions and just watching as the group members talk about pouring the Windex.)

options.A: Frame the biology investigation topics as problems that relate to how the student views herself in the present and in the future.
options.B: Use specific conceptual questions about the plant investigation with a limited range of possible answers rather than broad, open-ended questions.
options.C: Act as a role model in developing a warm classroom environment that places limits and consequences on unacceptable group behaviors.
options.D: Have the student use a digital notebook to take notes, organize her group work, and archive past biology projects.
